issues.reason: `Forbid` is defined only as the seal of a NEGATIVE IMPERATIVE, so pressing it into service as a polarity carrier inside the make_sure complement is exactly the invented encoding the registered no-polarity-inside-a-seal limitation forbids, and it records a prohibition on entering that the text never states.

The standing half is that "nobody" leaves no trace at all in the parse; the overstated half is the demanded carrier — a seal has no strength-0.0 slot and no `QuantifierPhrase` can live inside a term, and minting a `person` witness as the go event's Agent inside the seal would assert the very thing the sentence denies.

The "untyped referent symbol must never appear" rule governs witnesses minted for personal pronouns; a deictic locative pro-form follows the deictic-constant precedent instead (`now` / `yesterday` are bare constants that must NOT get a `Member` atom), so bare `there` is graceful improvisation in the reviewer's own gap territory.

The oblique table assigns `Location` to "in / at / on …" and the mechanical rule is to use the preposition actually used (`Goal` renders "to / into / onto"), and nothing bars a `Location` oblique on a motion event.

gaps_confirmed: "make sure / ensure that P": a finite that-clause complement of a verb that is neither a thought/speech attitude, an embedded question, an imperative nor a counterfactual — no sealing route covers it
a negative-quantifier subject inside a sealed complement — the registered no-polarity-carrier-inside-a-seal limitation extends here, so "nobody" is unrepresentable in that position
deictic locative pro-forms ("there", "here") — deictic times are given speech-anchored bare constants but no rule covers a deictic place
new_gaps: "goes in there": nothing decides whether "in" is the particle of a phrasal verb (`go_in`, kept whole, no genus) or a preposition heading its own oblique — the two give different symbols for the same clause

an imperative whose commanded content is itself a proposition ("make sure that P") needs a seal nested inside a seal; the sealing rule describes only one level, and the honest parse therefore loses the entire complement
repair_summary: Dropped the `(Theme … (Forbid …))` complement entirely: removing only the invented `Forbid` operator would leave a positively sealed "a going-in-there happens", which is the opposite of the sentence and would fail the calibration line, so the wholly-negated and unexpressible complement is left out per the registered limitation. Wrote the now single-atom seal in the licensed bare form (`a single atom as itself`) rather than a one-conjunct `(And …)`.
notes: The outer `Directive`, the tenseless addressee-free make_sure reification and the bare deictic `there` are all correct; the repair is severely lossy only because every contentful part of the complement is unrepresentable, which is the gap, not a parser failure.
